title: Christians alarmed as Pakistan’s largest province urges tougher ‘blasphemy’ penalties
description: Bringing you the news from a traditional Catholic perspective. ( LifeSiteNews ) — Religious freedom advocates in Pakistan warn that a legislative push in Punjab province to toughen penalties for religious speech offenses will hand extremists a stronger weapon against vulnerable Christians and other minorities. … Accusations involving remarks about Islamic figures have long carried grave consequences for Pakistani Christians. In 2009, Christian farmworker Asia Bibi was accused of insulting Prophet Muhammad during an argument with Muslim coworkers over a cup of water, spending eight years on death row before Pakistan’s Supreme Court acquitted her in 2018 amid violent nationwide protests. Unverified blasphemy allegations in Punjab also triggered the August 2023 riots in Jaranwala, in Faisalabad district, t The global volatility around perceived insults to early Islamic figures surfaced in 1988 with British novelist Salman Rushdie’s The Satanic Verses . Though Rushdie is not Christian, his controversial references to Muhammad and his wives ignited global protests, deadly riots in Pakistan, and a 1989 religious edict calling for the author’s death, demonstrating how accusations tied to Islamic sacred figures can rapidly escalate into transnational unrest. Pakistan ranked eighth on Open Doors’ 2026 World Watch List of countries where Christians face the most severe persecution. Rights defenders warn that elevating penalties under Section 298-A will deepen fear among Christian families across Pakistan and further embolden vigilante groups.
